source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Shrub or small tree, rarely reaches 10 m
morphology_documented.leaves: Usually (3–)5–9 glabrous strongly veined ovate-lanceolate leaflets, terminal ones sometimes partially fused
morphology_documented.flowers: Fragrant before or with foliage; four or five rose-pink/purple petals, hairy claw, seven to ten stamens with red anthers
morphology_documented.fruit: Three-lobed capsule 3.5–5 cm, pale green sometimes reddish, glossy dark seeds 10–15 mm

source_scope_note: Historic taxonomic rank maintained; comparative key traits or family-only descriptions not automatically promoted to accepted species level.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Despite name Mexican buckeye, it differs from Aesculus by alternate pinnate rather than opposite palmately compound leaves
preservation: Additive species source references only; no original records, photos, credits or galleries changed
